item.research_question: What is the minimum level of thermodynamic assessment (specifically regarding ternary systems) required to correctly predict the thermodynamic properties and phase equilibria of quaternary high entropy alloys using CALPHAD?
item.material_system: Co-Cr-Fe-Ni (FAB=1, FAT=1), Co-Cu-Fe-Ni (FAB=1, FAT=1), and Al-Co-Ni-Ti (FAB=1, FAT=3/4)
item.processing_route: CALPHAD calculations using the TCHEA3 database; reference states (FAT=1 or 3/4) were compared against artificially reduced states (FAT=0) where all ternary interaction parameters were set to zero or ternary intermetallics were suspended, while binary parameters remained fully assessed.
item.test_conditions: Calculations performed at 800 °C for Co-Cr-Fe-Ni; 12,341 equally spaced system points with 2.5 at.% compositional steps were analyzed across the quaternary composition space.
key_findings: In Co-Cr-Fe-Ni, 98% of fcc and bcc phase points calculated with FAT=0 matched the FAT=1 reference predictions.
In Co-Cu-Fe-Ni, only 63% of fcc phase points matched between FAT=0 and FAT=1 due to incorrect miscibility gap boundaries, while bcc phase agreement was nearly 100%.
In Al-Co-Ni-Ti, FAT=0 calculations failed to predict ternary intermetallic phases (H_L21, Laves_C14), filling those regions with binary phases instead.
Disagreements between FAT=0 and FAT=1 calculations occur primarily at or near the boundaries between different phase-field regions.
Systems with low density of phase boundaries (few intermetallics, no miscibility gaps) show negligible sensitivity to the removal of ternary descriptions.
The presence of ternary intermetallic phases in the system causes significant shifts in the composition and boundaries of neighboring phase regions when ternary interactions are neglected.
item.mechanism: The accuracy of extrapolation depends on the thermodynamic properties of the subsystems; near-ideal mixtures (like Co-Cr-Fe-Ni) have negligible ternary contributions to Gibbs free energy, whereas systems with miscibility gaps or ternary intermetallics rely heavily on ternary interaction parameters to correctly define phase boundaries and phase stability.
item.limitations: The study is limited to quaternary systems and relies on a single commercial database (TCHEA3); the authors note that locations of phase boundaries and ternary phases are unknown in novel composition spaces, making it difficult to apply these criteria a priori.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the conclusions for quaternary alloys can be extended to higher order systems, but emphasize that calculations using lower credibility databases require additional experimental verification.
quotes: The main differences in the calculations occur at or near the boundaries between different phase fields. Therefore, higher density of these boundaries should result in lower accuracy of the FAT = 0 calculations.

Because the locations of the phase boundaries and possibility of formation of ternary phases are not known when evaluating novel composition space, a higher credibility database is still preferable, while the calculations using lower credibility databases may be questionable and require additional experimental verification.
